name: f33_boot_eiint_vector
review_result: Boot EIINT entry: SYNCP then branch to context-save body 10C. Executed through real state1 timer callback and EIRET; no normal C arguments or return contract. FPEC=0 and manually seeded architectural interrupt context; not physical interrupt acquisition or timing.

name: f33_boot_eiint_context
review_result: Save r6/EIPC/EIPSW; read EIIC into r6; EI; save r1..lp; call 748; restore GPRs; DI; restore EIPSW/EIPC/r6; EIRET. Full execution preserves all 31 GPRs and stack canaries; restores PSW and clears ISPR. Pending-FPI and nested-interrupt behavior are not exercised.

name: f33_boot_dispatch_eiic
review_result: Walk eight-byte EIIC/handler records from TP=869C until exact cause or FFFFFFFF sentinel; call selected handler. Eight records include the default. Cause27F selects default1EA4 despite a following 27F/32A0 pair; that pair is not part of this traversal. Boot timer1087 executes through 1E44. No physical interrupt routing experiment.

name: f33_boot_tauj0_ch2_callback
review_result: Boot callback for EIIC1087: TAUJ0 channel2 per P1M-E R01UH0585EJ0120 page284. Calls1CE8 ->1E04 ->14A2; state byteFEBF2904==2 enters services while state1 returns. Exact state1 chain and interrupt return executed without callee replacement; state2 services and physical scheduling are not exercised.

name: f33_boot_copy_flash_driver_to_ram
review_result: Boot phase: copies exactly 0xCB words from CodeFlash 0x8370..0x869B to RAM 0xFEBF1000..0xFEBF132B, reads back the last word, SYNCM/SYNCI. Full copied span and both canaries executed. RAM callback FEBF12B8 maps to ROM 8628 only in this phase; application crypto reuses the RAM. Physical cache timing is not established.

name: f33_boot_cache_set_enabled
review_result: Low-byte zero disables data buffer/instruction cache before clearing; nonzero clears then enables. CDBCLR reads zero while ICHCLR completion is asynchronous. Exact136-byte processor fixture checks command/read behavior and reachable high-IR effects/polls/return. Execution explicitly injects completion; SYNCI remains opaque and the shared return instruction is exercised separately. No physical cache contents or latency claim.

name: f33_read_repair_redundant_u8
review_result: Vote three XOR-encoded byte cells. Status0 returns without repair; -11/-12 republish the voted value; all other failures republish low8(fallback). Invalid pointers make the publisher reject without partial stores while the wrapper still returns fallback. Final LD.BU zero-extends the full r10 result. Real voter and publisher execute, not replacements; no physical interrupt interleaving claim.

name: f33_copy_whole_words
review_result: Copy floor(low16(byte_count)/4) words forward from r7 to r6; ignore trailing bytes. No pointer/alignment validation or return-value contract. Executed low16 truncation, tails and forward-overlap propagation; not memmove and not a byte-complete copy.

name: f33_update_whole_words
review_result: Same forward whole-word extent as66E2E, but store only differing words and return full-register0/1 for whether any differed. Sticky result remains1 when the final word already matches. Boundary sweep also exercised zero/short counts, low16 truncation and overlap; no alignment-fault or physical timing claim.

name: f33_priority_mask_enter
review_result: Return old PMR; replace it only when signed32(old)<signed32(requested). Write path preserves incoming PSW.ID and executes SYNCP. Not bitwise union or unconditional interrupt disable. Direct execution covers lower/equal/higher masks and signed-negative request with both ID states; FPEC=0, no asynchronous interrupt or reserved-register-bit claim.

name: f33_priority_mask_restore
review_result: Unconditionally write saved PMR, preserve incoming PSW.ID around the write, then SYNCP; no return contract. Both ID states executed directly and through real publishers. Preserving ID does not mean restoring every PSW flag; pending-FPI behavior and physical interrupt exclusion are outside these runs.

name: f33_vote_redundant_u8
review_result: Reject any NULL or output==raw with-1 and no output write. Snapshot raw and55/AA-encoded bytes under PMRFFC0; normalize. All agree:0/raw; raw agrees with either copy:-11/raw; encoded pair agrees:-12/pair; all differ:-13/raw, still writing output. Output may alias either encoded input; only the output cell is written. All single-bit faults in each lane exercised for six base values.

name: f33_publish_redundant_u8
review_result: Any NULL destination returns-1 before all stores. Otherwise write low8(value), value^55 and value^AA in that order under the real PMRFFC0 enter/restore pair, then return0. Upper value bits discarded; no alias rejection. Sweep covers each NULL position and both ID states; not globally atomic storage.

name: f33_publish_redundant_u16
review_result: Any NULL destination returns-1 without partial stores. Otherwise write low16(value), value^5555 and value^AAAA in that order under the real PMRFFC0 pair, then return0. No alias rejection or local alignment check. Executed narrowing, both ID states and each NULL position; no hardware-interleaving proof.

name: f33_nvm_payload_length
review_result: Zero-extended payload length from27636+6*low16(handle). No local bound check. All123 registered indices executed; descriptor1 is16 bytes, not the preceding sentinel descriptor's32. Full-body register dataflow preserves r7/r8; real p-code inlining restores their forwarding in748E4.

name: f33_nvm_base_offset
review_result: Read unsigned page at27634+6*low16(handle), return page<<6. No local bound or sentinel rejection; descriptor0 returns003FFFC0. All123 registered indices executed. Preserves r7/r8; no claim that sentinel output is a valid physical DataFlash address.

name: f33_nvm_descriptor_option
review_result: LD.BU reads option byte27638+6*low16(handle), zero-extended inr10. All123 registered options are zero. Raw field offset and full register preservation established; composed execution traverses the real getter. OEM option-bit meanings and nonzero registered configurations are not recovered.

name: f33_nvm_allocation_pages
review_result: Allocation pages=(payload_len+(payload_len>32?4:0)+(option!=0?12:4)+64)>>6. Includes record overhead, unlike77314. All nine registered length classes executed; length64 requires2 allocation pages. Full body and callees preserve r7/r8, requiring real p-code inlining for the caller's forwarded inputs. No flash programming executed.

name: f33_nvm_record_offset
review_result: Three explicit arguments: low16(handle), low16(allocation_index), uint32 byte_offset. Return base_offset + allocation_index*allocation_pages*64 + byte_offset with native32-bit arithmetic. All123 descriptor indices and upper-bit truncation executed without replacing helpers. Allocation index is a structural term, not a recovered logical-copy identity.

name: f33_nvm_payload_page_count
review_result: For payload length n return (((n+(n&3))&FFFF)+60)>>6. All nine registered length classes executed; a64-byte payload returns1 while allocation_pages returns2. Registered lengths are multiples of eight; do not replace literal arithmetic with generic rounding for arbitrary lengths.

name: f33_nvm_trailer_offset
review_result: Return allocation_pages*64-4. Every registered length class executed; length248 has a5-page allocation and trailer offset316. 77AA8 reads this location and comparesAAAAAAAA. Marker presence is not checksum validation or logical copy consensus.

name: FUN_00077982
review_result: Unsigned low16 handle must be below the bound at27928 (123); rejected handles return0000FFFB. Both123 andFFFF executed on the rejection path. Admitted inputs delegate base offset and allocation pages to77650/74B76. This review does not assign the underlying hardware-job role or establish successful flash operation.

name: f33_memcpy_forward
review_result: Forward byte-counted copy: r6 destination, r7 source, r8 byte count; returns original destination in r10. Word path requires both pointers four-byte aligned; otherwise byte path. Exact firmware execution covers aligned bulk/tail and unaligned copies, unchanged source, destination canaries and stack restoration. Not an overlap-safe memmove contract.

name: f33_memzero
review_result: Byte-counted zero fill: r6 destination, r7 byte count, no return contract. Short unaligned and 128-byte-block-plus-tail paths execute with exact destination and canary checks. Uses byte alignment prelude, 128/64/32/16-byte blocks and word/byte tails; zero count makes no destination write in the separate exhaustive boundary smoke.

name: f33_freshness_encode_wire
review_result: Encode 4-bit or 46-bit freshness into one or six MSB-first bytes. Capacity admission compares only the low byte of the uint32 in/out capacity. Insufficient capacity preserves output and capacity; otherwise unsupported format sets capacity zero without writing output. Supported output reports bit length and zeroes unused trailing wire bits. Exact execution checks both formats, low-byte capacity rejection, unsupported format, source preservation and canaries.

name: f33_freshness_decode_wire
review_result: Decode exact bit lengths 4 and 46 into a 12-byte wire record: trip32 +0, reset32 +4, message16 +8, reset-low2 +10, bit length +11. Truncated format reads one byte and zeroes trip/reset; full format reads six bytes containing 16/20/8/2 bits. Unsupported full-word lengths zero the entire record without reading input. Execution checks unused wire bits, unaligned source, exact initialized source extent, canaries and an unmapped unsupported-format source. This decoder's zero marker is not a complete transaction rejection.

name: f33_freshness_select_reset_candidate
review_result: Ordered reset search reloads FEBE55C4 each attempt and considers current,-1,+1,-2,+2 within 0..0xFFFFF. Match low bits and skip the requested unsigned16 matching ordinal; return 1 with candidate/index or 0 when exhausted. Failed candidate value is unspecified. Exact execution checks ambiguous -2/+2 selection and both counter boundaries. Raw 909CA..90A47 preserves r6-r9; sole caller 90B76 forwards them at 90B7E. Inline real p-code to retain that actual register dataflow rather than imposing generic caller-saved kills.

name: f33_freshness_reconstruct_ordinary
review_result: Read current trip and selected committed history; newer trip/reset seeds message from received low bits. Same epoch rebuilds message congruence and optionally advances one interval. Reset ceiling or message overflow yields message FF with return 0; the outer wrapper interprets the sentinel. Older epoch returns 0x23 while candidate index <4, otherwise 0x22, without output writes. Successful output writes ten bytes and preserves the opaque tail. Executed new-epoch low2 values 0..3, wrap, saturation, stale epochs and width8 behavior; retained fixtures protect distinct boundaries.

name: f33_freshness_reconstruct_candidate
review_result: Compose ordered reset search and message reconstruction using explicit output pointer r9. Message width is clamp(bit_length-2,0,8); reset-low width is two except input bit lengths 0 or1 are retained. Matching ordinal can move an older -2 candidate returning 0x23 to an admissible +2 candidate. No candidate returns 0x22 without output writes. A zeroed unsupported-format parse record is not independently rejected here: the executed new-epoch case reconstructs message0. This is a direct helper boundary, not proof of CAN or authenticated-transaction admission.

name: f33_freshness_commit_pending
review_result: For unsigned slot <2 and low-byte result ==1, copy 12 bytes from pending FEBE55F4+12*slot to committed FEBE55DC+12*slot inside the ordinary critical section. Executed second-slot commit, invalid slot rejection, nonboolean result rejection and low-byte truncation; pending source and nesting count preserved. Not rollback and not PDU dequeue.

name: f33_curve16_interpolate_with_slope
review_result: Sixteen signed-x/unsigned-y points in a 0x44-byte row; last four bytes not read. Upper clamp uses point15; lower inputs extrapolate segment0. Interpolated value narrows to unsigned16 with signed16 denominator. Signed16 second output blends maxima of neighboring quantized slopes and rescales Q8 to Q9 without saturation; duplicate-x slope fallback comes from AF88C. 54 exact-image executions cover real-row knots and boundaries plus duplicate-x fallbacks. Physical units and all malformed-table/native arithmetic exceptional cases remain outside the executed boundary.
